title: Turn flow: question, retrieval, agent loop, tools
description: One turn end to end, for debugging and security operations. Spans come from app/security/telemetry/spans.ts. Structural attributes (counts, labels, statuses) are always exported. Question text, evidence paths and tool arguments appear only on a developer stack with TELEMETRY_DEBUG_CONTENT=1 and APP_ENV local or test; uat and production refuse to start with that flag, and a deployed collector does not allowlist those attributes.

panels.title: Turns: pick one to open its flow
panels.description: One row per turn span. run_handle matches the run the interface shows and the turns table, so a turn can be followed from here into the application. Click the trace id for the waterfall: turn, scope, retrieval, each agent round, each tool.

targets.query: { name = "turn" } | select(span.app.turn.run_handle, span.app.turn.scope_label, span.app.turn.run_state, span.app.turn.reason, span.app.retrieval.seed_source, span.app.retrieval.status, span.app.retrieval.items, span.app.turn.question)

panels.title: Agent rounds: what each round did and why it ended
panels.description: One row per round of the tool loop. stop_reason says how the round ended: tool_use (it asked for tools), end_turn, iterations, deadline, aborted, model_error, output_blocked, or tool_budget_exhausted when the cap refused a sixth round.

targets.query: { name = "agent.round" } | select(span.app.agent.round, span.app.agent.stop_reason, span.app.agent.tools_requested, span.app.agent.iterations, span.app.error.code)

panels.title: Tool calls: what the model asked the agent for
panels.description: One row per tool the model requested and the agent executed, with the round it belongs to and how it ended. status: ok, timeout, error, refused, unknown, or index for a pre-run the system ran before the model's first turn. Arguments appear only on a developer stack.

panels.title: The full request the model was sent (developer stack only)
panels.description: Tempo truncates a span attribute at 2048 bytes, so app.model.messages on the turn span carries the opening of the request and a count of what was cut. The whole array is here, stamped with the trace and span id by the OpenTelemetry bridge: expand a line, or add | trace_id="..." to pin it to the turn above. Present only on a developer stack, where TELEMETRY_DEBUG_CONTENT is set and APP_ENV is local or test; everywhere else the record is never written and the body limit of 160 bytes applies as it does to every other log.

panels.title: Model calls: the provider leg of each round
panels.description: The outbound call to the gateway. Duration here against the round duration above separates model latency from tool latency.

panels.title: Turns per minute, by scope and outcome
panels.description: app_turns_total, split by the scope the classifier assigned, the state the run ended in, and whether the evidence gate released the answer.

panels.title: Withheld by the evidence gate, by mechanism
panels.description: app_gate_withheld_total. A mechanism appearing here that is not a quoted comment means a budget or the verifier removed the last piece of evidence for a sentence.

panels.title: Security events on the turn path (click trace to open the flow)
panels.description: The catalogued events a turn can raise: injection.suspected, answer.claim_withheld, policy.enforced, canary.followed, question.url_requested, content.url_masked, content.pii_masked, egress.forbidden, error.unhandled. Fields are catalogue-capped, so no request content rides here regardless of the developer flag.
